tools.name: fuzzframe_action
tools.description: Runs any of Fuzzframe's actions by name, including ones newer than the tools your chat knows (a chat keeps its own copy of a connector's tools for a while). action "list": every action now, each with what it does and its arguments as JSON Schema. tools.name: plan

tools.name: look_stills
tools.description: Shows the person three looks with the video's own cover headline on each, in one card, with colours to try under the one they choose, "From a reference" and "See all". tools.name: notes_heard

tools.name: brief

tools.name: plan_series
tools.description: Saves a series the person approved: its name, what it's about and for whom, what every episode is made with (kind, look, voice, length, tone, music, language) and the episodes in order (title, first line, angle, points). tools.description: What this person likes in a video, learned from their own choices and reviews: their account's taste, and a series' taste when the video belongs to one (the series wins where both say something). Read it before planning a video and follow it over the look's defaults. Also lists their series.

tools.name: remember_taste
tools.description: Saves something about this person's taste, only when THEY ask for it to be remembered for a series or for all their videos ("always", "for this series", "from now on"); a note on one video is fixed in that video and not remembered. Dials move one step at a time relative to the look's defaults.

tools.name: start_video
tools.description: Creates the video in the person's Fuzzframe account and records the voiceover once (this uses their credits: the brief's Make it is the OK in make it for me; in choose each step, picking the voice is the OK to record; a second take is asked again first). The film is timed on this take, so the script

tools.name: video
tools.description: Where a video stands: the word timings, the film's files and whether they compile, the studio link to watch it, and the export's progress or MP4 link.

tools.name: save_storyboard
tools.description: Shows the person the storyboard as a card to approve (a timeline on the recorded take, each beat with its time, words, on-screen plan and a sketch in the film's colours; once a plan is saved with save_animatic, a real rough frame of each beat, drawn from the plan before any film code exists) and kee

tools.name: stage
tools.description: The instructions for one stage of making a film, with the rules that apply to it. Call it when the guide says, and follow what it returns for that stage.

tools.name: save_animatic
tools.description: Saves the film's storyboard as data (the animatic: beats on the recorded words, grid anchors, camera, transitions, events) with the look's tokens, and checks it. Every [fail] must be fixed and the plan saved again before any film code is written.

tools.name: qa_film
tools.description: Renders the film's keyframes from the saved plan and measures them: safe zones, overlaps, clipping, type sizes, contrast, the cover, and the code's timing, colours and easing. Each [fail] is objective: fix them all with edit_file and measure again. Run it after typecheck is clean.

tools.name: save_critique
tools.description: Saves the one technical look at the film's contact sheets (glitches, collisions code can't measure, the picture not matching the voice, a beat that doesn't do the motion its plan invented: kind flat). Once per film.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Writes one file of the film (film/Film.tsx is the entry) and compiles the whole film. Returns what is wrong, or that it plays. Use edit_file for small changes afterwards.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replaces one exact piece of text in a film file (it must occur exactly once) and compiles the film.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: A film file as it is saved now.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Removes a film file that is no longer used, and compiles the film.

tools.name: typecheck
tools.description: Checks the film's TypeScript against the kit (wrong props, missing names, wrong types): the mistakes compiling alone doesn't catch. Run it before the first stills and after big changes.

tools.name: stills
tools.description: Renders frames of the film at the given seconds and returns them as one labelled sheet for you to LOOK at. Small (up to 12 frames, for the whole film) or large (up to 6, to read text and judge detail).

tools.name: pictures
tools.description: Draws pictures for a motion film on fal and links them to the video, so the film shows the thing itself (a person, a building, a product, an animal, a scene) and never a placeholder. kind "cutout": one subject on a transparent background, trimmed to it, to move like a paper puppet; kind "backdrop":

tools.name: link_asset
tools.description: Puts a picture from the person's library (assets) on this video under a name the film finds it by (useFilm().assets); the library shows that name too. Free.

tools.name: recipe
tools.description: A whole film built only from Fuzzframe's kit pieces, with its rules (pacing, palette, which piece when): start from it when the chosen look has one, keep its pieces and camera language, and put the person's words and timings in. Without a name, lists the recipes.

tools.name: music

tools.description: Puts the voiceover in a space: "room" (Room), "slapback" (Slapback), "echo-throw" (Echo throw), "big-space" (Big space), or "none". tools.name: review
tools.description: Renders one frame per scene of the film as it is now and shows the person a review card: each scene's frame, time and words, with quick notes to tap or type per scene and for the whole film, and where to remember them (this video, the series, all their videos). Stage "draft" when it's ready to watch

tools.description: Renders the current version in HD (1080×1920, 60 fps). Uses the person's credits like any export: the brief's Make it is the OK in make it for me; in choose each step, Export on the draft card (or their saying export) is the OK to export. Any export after the first MP4 is asked again first. A versio

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "brief" appears informational but accepts parameters (script) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: kind, look, look_name, colours, voice_id, voice_name, length, music, title, first_line, estimate, ideas, script, scenes, characters, lettering, texture, mood, voice_pace, voice_tone, voice_search, sound_effects, ambience, captions, on_screen_text, ending, shape

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "write_file" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "read_file" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fuzzframe_action, voices, save_voice, brief, story_looks, contact_support, taste, pictures · Private data: start_story, story, contact_support, start_video, video, save_animatic, save_critique, write_file, edit_file, read_file, delete_file, assets · Public sink: post_text, assets, music · Destructive: brief, contact_support, qa_film, delete_file, typecheck, fal_models, fal_run.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fuzzframe_action, voices, save_voice, brief, story_looks, contact_support, taste, pictures · Private data: start_story, story, contact_support, start_video, video, save_animatic, save_critique, write_file, edit_file, read_file, delete_file, assets · Public sink: post_text, assets, music · Destructive: brief, contact_support, qa_film, delete_file, typecheck, fal_models, fal_run

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
